The enhancement would introduce:

- A bounded worker pool for workspace queries.
- Cancellation through scheduling and retrieval.
- Deterministic output, preserving each repository’s ranking and grouping.
- Retained errors and source isolation when individual members fail.
- Benchmarks covering latency, peak memory, and worker limits.

I found **four substantial feature candidates** across Brain, CLI, Git Sync, and ForgeMark. **These remain proposals requiring validation—not four implementation-cleared tasks.** The Brain candidate has the strongest measured evidence.

1. **ENH-004 — Brain: persistent memory search index**

   Make repeated searches reuse an on-disk lexical index instead of loading and rescoring the entire memory collection each time.

   My fresh test queried **50,000 synthetic facts and returned one result in a median 1.06 seconds**, including about **0.75 seconds of BM25 scoring**. This is separate from ENH-001’s concurrency across repositories. [Measurement log](/Users/puneetpalsingh/.codex/entire-big-features-2026-11-13/memory-index-baseline.log).

   The engineering work includes incremental index updates, atomic publication, stale-index detection, deletion handling, and preserving existing ranking, Unicode tokenization, filters, and provenance.

   **Overlap:** current code already identifies an inverted index as a possible future upgrade. I found no exact active implementation in the scoped checks; this is a known design direction, not an original discovery. [Current scorer](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/blob/834fbc88c950412c9e19b8b4cf6129e457094cba/internal/cli/facts_bm25.go).

2. **ENH-005 — CLI: reproducible project plugin environments**

   Let a repository declare a reproducible set of plugin versions and checksums, then explicitly synchronize that environment on developer machines and CI. Different projects could use different versions concurrently.

   This would require dependency resolution, multiple installed versions, project-specific dispatch, trusted activation, Windows support, and careful handling of plugin data-schema compatibility.

   **Overlap:** Entire already supports individual global pins and dependencies through [#1422](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1422). [#3074](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/3074) adds installation mutexes and rollback. Neither supplies a project plugin environment. I found no exact implementation in the scoped searches, but demand and the compatibility contract need confirmation.

3. **ENH-006 — Git Sync: saved plans with controlled execution**

   Allow someone to generate a concrete synchronization plan, review it, and later execute **that exact set of ref updates**.

   Today, `Plan` previews work and `Sync` independently plans again. The new capability would bind source/target identities, ref hashes, mappings, and policies into a versioned artifact. Execution would reject stale plans and produce per-ref receipts, including partial failures. [Current API](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/blob/67dd3a4e083e4faae4417c1849035c7c4638112c/client.go).

   **Overlap:** [#123](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/123) addresses concurrent ref safety. That protection must be preserved; the proposed feature adds a persisted review-to-execution contract. No exact saved-plan implementation surfaced in the checks.

4. **ENH-007 — ForgeMark: distributed benchmarks across multiple machines**

   Run one benchmark workload across remote workers and combine their results, so the load generator can scale beyond one machine.

   The work includes worker registration, coordinated measurement windows, unique ref namespaces, worker-local credentials, latency aggregation, cancellation, and explicit reporting when workers disappear.

   ForgeMark’s README already identifies generator CPU saturation as a measurement limit. Its current coordinator runs targets within one process. [Current documentation](https://github.com/entireio/forgemark).

**My recommendation:** investigate **Brain’s persistent memory index next**. It has measurable cost and a direct connection to agent context assembly. **Git Sync’s saved-plan execution** is the strongest separate systems feature to validate.

**1. ENH-009 — CI failure-and-recovery memory in Brain — my first choice**

Let Brain remember failures from RWX/Dagger runs and retrieve relevant past recoveries during future coding tasks.

Example: an agent encounters a migration failure. Brain returns a previous occurrence, its environment, the fixing commit and the successful follow-up run.

The substantial work would include:

- Repository, commit, run and retry-attempt identity.
- Deduplicated imports and interrupted-import recovery.
- Source citations, redaction and stale-evidence handling.
- Distinguishing a suspected fix from one supported by a subsequent passing run.

Brain already mines session failures, and [#595](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/595) owns review-memory provenance. **Our proposed addition would specifically ingest external CI evidence**, reusing those contracts. Start with one provider and structured test results.

**2. ENH-010 — A regression evaluation kit for custom review agents**

Teams can create review agents today. Add a way to measure whether changing their instructions or model improves review quality.

Run two reviewer configurations against the same labeled collection of buggy and clean patches. Report:

- Bugs detected and missed.
- False alarms on clean code.
- Whether cited locations support findings.
- Cost, latency and variation across repeated runs.

This would help answer: “Did our new security-review prompt improve detection, or just generate more findings?”

Existing [CLI #2338](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2338) covers local review preview. This proposal adds a **labeled regression corpus and comparative evaluation**, beyond previewing a review. It could begin as a companion plugin.

Example policy: “Release tags matching `v*` may be created once; subsequent movement or deletion must fail this audit—even if the original target is later restored.”

The feature would evaluate multiple refs, produce violations linked to exact RSL entries, and generate a CI-consumable report. It needs careful handling of trusted baselines, annotations, incomplete history and verification failures.

RSL already supplies inspection and cryptographic verification. This proposal adds **consumer-defined historical rules**. ## Git and subprocess safety

- Open repositories only through `gitrepo.OpenCurrent(ctx)` or
  `gitrepo.OpenPath(root)`, never direct go-git opens. This preserves alternates
  and reftable support. Do not fall back to CWD after failed repo resolution.

- Every `git status` subprocess passes **`--no-optional-locks`**. This does not
  protect worktree-comparing `git diff` from refreshing the index; use the
  hook-safe alternatives in the git reference.
- Use the git CLI, not go-git v5, for checkout and hard reset; go-git can delete
  ignored/untracked directories. This is an implementation rule, not permission

### Summary

`entire checkpoint explain --session <id>` applies a default scan limit, but when that limit truncates the scan it reports **zero checkpoints in definitive language** rather than reporting truncation. The output simultaneously claims the history is empty and admits it may be hidden:

```
  branch       <branch>
  session      <session-id>
  checkpoints  0

No checkpoints found on this branch.
Checkpoints will appear here after you save changes during an agent session.
note: checkpoint list reached its scan limit; older checkpoints may be hidden. Run 'entire checkpoint explain --json --limit <N>' to see more.
```

The same command with an explicit limit returns the checkpoints immediately:

```
entire checkpoint explain --session <id> --json --limit 2000
→ [ { "checkpoint_id": "…", "session_id": "…", "agent": "Claude Code", … }, … ]
```

So the data is present and reachable. Only the default-limit path misreports it.

### Why this matters more than a cosmetic wording issue

The headline (`checkpoints 0` + `No checkpoints found`) and the footnote (`older checkpoints may be hidden`) contradict each other, and the wrong half is the prominent one. A human may read down to the note. **An agent generally does not.**

This bites the search skill that Entire itself installs (`--search-skill`, `ENTIRE-MANAGED SEARCH SKILL v1`). Observed live: a subagent following the shipped v1 prompt concluded

> "the accessible session transcripts in Entire don't contain the diagnostic discussion … the decision-making appears to have been done post-hoc in commit messages rather than during an interactive session transcript that Entire captured."

That was false. The session file held **306** matches for the search term, and `--limit 2000` returned the checkpoints at once. The agent reported absence of history as a finding, with no signal to the user that the lookup had been truncated.

Step 5 of the shipped v1 prompt compounds it:

> "If nothing looks right, rerun a narrower `entire search --json --compact` instead of explaining many hits or switching tools."

When the cause of "nothing looks like it exists" is a silent truncation, *narrowing* is exactly the wrong recovery — it makes the false negative more confident. The prompt has no instruction to raise the limit before concluding absence.

### Environment

* Entire CLI **0.10.2** (go1.26.6, darwin/arm64)
* Checkpoint backend: `git-refs`
* Agents: Claude Code + Codex
* ~900 checkpoints in the repo, created by the history import that `entire enable` offers (`Imported 921 turn(s) from 29 session(s)`)
* Private GitHub repo; all checkpoint refs confirmed pushed to origin

Possibly relevant: the imported checkpoints carry `"is_logs_only": true`, and some `message` fields are terminal scrollback rather than prompts. I did not test whether the same truncation reports zero on natively-captured (non-imported) checkpoints.

### Reproduction

1. Enable Entire on a repo with substantial agent history, accepting the history import at `enable` (enough to exceed the default scan limit — ~900 checkpoints here).
2. Pick a session id known to contain matching content.
3. `entire checkpoint explain --session <id>` → `checkpoints 0`, `No checkpoints found on this branch.`
4. `entire checkpoint explain --session <id> --json --limit 2000` → checkpoints returned.

### Suggested fixes

Any one of these would remove the false negative; the first two seem most valuable:

1. **Do not print `No checkpoints found` when the scan was truncated.** If the limit was hit and zero matched, that is an *inconclusive* result, not an empty one. Say so in the headline — e.g. `checkpoints 0 of ≥N scanned (scan limit reached — pass --limit to widen)`.
2. **Make the `--json` shape carry it.** A `"truncated": true` / `"scan_limit_reached": true` field would let agents detect this programmatically instead of relying on prose in a note they don't read.
3. **Auto-widen once** when a `--session`-scoped lookup returns zero and the limit was hit, since a session-scoped query has a naturally bounded result set.
4. **Update the shipped search skill** to require an explicit high-limit lookup before an agent may state that history has no match. (Patched locally, but it is an `ENTIRE-MANAGED` file, so a `--force` reinstall or a v2 skill will silently overwrite the fix.)

### Related

Adjacent but distinct from #1195 — there, `entire search` returns 0 while `checkpoint explain` sees the data. Here it is `checkpoint explain` itself under-reporting. I also saw search return only `type: "commit"` hits while matching transcripts existed, which may be the same surface as #1195.
